[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 03:41  
[USER] User asked how to create a 3D sphere using Spline software.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To create a 3D sphere using Spline software, start by launching Spline and creating a new project.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 3D view, select the "Create" tab in the toolbar and then click on the "Sphere" icon.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This will bring up the "Create Sphere" dialog box, where you can specify the radius of the sphere and the number of segments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Once you have set the desired parameters, click on the "Create" button to create the sphere.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The sphere will appear in the 3D view, and you can use various tools in Spline to manipulate it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The sphere will be created as a mesh object, which is a collection of vertices, edges, and faces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] You can use the "Edit" tab in the toolbar to modify the shape of the sphere by moving individual vertices or manipulating edges and faces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] You can also use the "Material" tab to apply textures and colors to the sphere.  
[USER] User asked how to turn the 3D sphere into a Mickey Mouse.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To turn a 3D sphere into a Mickey Mouse character, start by scaling the sphere to the desired size for Mickey Mouse's head using the "Scale" tool in the "Edit" tab.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Move" tool to position the sphere for Mickey Mouse's head orientation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Extrude" tool to create the shape of Mickey Mouse's ears by selecting the faces of the sphere that will become the ears.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Subdivide" tool to add more detail and resolution to the ears.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Smooth" tool to smooth out the surface of the ears.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Move" tool to position the ears correctly on the head.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Extrude" tool to create the nose and mouth by pulling out the appropriate faces of the sphere.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Subdivide" and "Smooth" tools to refine the shape of the nose and mouth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use the "Move" tool to position the nose and mouth correctly on the head.
